Standard: For crewmembers that move throughout the air vehicle during flight with open doors or ramps, a mobile restraint system provides crash retention and fall protection. The mobile restraint system includes a torso harness and adjustable lanyard designed to distribute loads on the user during dynamic events. The mobile restraint system withstands a 5,000-lb static load. The mobile restraint system includes an emergency single-handed release that permits rapid release. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine the results of the drop testing and verify that no portion of the harness or restraint contacts the neck of the ATD or body block.
(2) Examine the results of the drop testing and verify that the system retains the ATD or body block. Verify that adjusters do not slip more than 1 inch, and the emergency release functions after exposure to loading. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Verification of mobile crewmember restraint performance includes static testing, drop testing, and dynamic testing utilizing body blocks or ATDs in representative initial conditions.
  (2) Lab test: Drop tests evaluate falls to full-lanyard length and dynamic crash tests verify the capability of the restraint to retain an occupant during velocity changes of at least 33 ft/s.
